gloss: in front of, before, opposite; tell, declare, make known; leader
summary: The root is being in front, in plain view. נֶגֶד is “in front of, before, opposite”: what stands before a man’s eyes or before Yahweh, where nothing is hidden. The verb, used only in the hiphil and hophal, is to put a matter in front of someone: to tell, report, explain a riddle or dream, own up to a sin, and above all, of Yahweh, to declare what is to come before it happens, which the idols cannot do (Isa 41:22–23; 46:10). נָגִיד is the one in front, the leader: the man Yahweh sets over his people (Saul, David, Solomon), the chief of the house of God, and the “anointed one, a leader” of Dan 9:25. In the Aramaic of Daniel the preposition is “toward” and the verb “flow”, and in the Peshitta the verb is to draw, lead or drag, and to scourge.

words.gloss: (hiphil) tell, report, declare, make known; (hophal) be told
words.summary: About 370 times, only in the hiphil (הִגִּיד) and its passive the hophal (הֻגַּד): there is no qal. To tell is to bring a matter out in front of the hearer, so that what he did not know, or what was hidden, is now before him. Its regular opposite is כִּחֵד “hide” (1Sa 3:18; Jos 7:19), and its regular partner in Isaiah is הִשְׁמִיעַ “make hear”.

stems.gloss: tell, report; make known (what is hidden); own up to, testify; declare (God’s word; what is to come; his praise)

senses.definition: To bring to someone’s knowledge something he does not know: news, what has happened, who one is. The one told is marked with לְ.

evidence.note: “Who told (הִגִּיד) you that you were naked?”: the man knows something he could only have learned.
וַיַּגֶּד־לוֹ שְׁמוּאֵל אֶת־כָּל־הַדְּבָרִים וְלֹא כִחֵד מִמֶּנּוּ: Samuel told Eli all the words and hid nothing from him.
Esther had not told her people or her kindred, for Mordecai had charged her not to tell: not telling is keeping it unknown.
Ham saw his father’s nakedness and told his two brothers outside.
Jacob told Rachel that he was her father’s kinsman, and she ran and told her father.
Jacob stole away from Laban “by not telling him that he was fleeing”.
The brothers told Jacob, “Joseph is still alive.”
The woman ran and told her husband that the man had appeared to her.
One told David that Ahithophel was among the conspirators.
The watchman called and told the king.
The sailors to Jonah: “Tell us, please, on whose account this evil is on us.”
“Only I alone have escaped to tell you.”
A bird of the heavens will carry the voice, and a winged thing will tell the matter.

senses.gloss: make known, explain (a riddle, a dream, a secret)
senses.definition: To lay open what is hidden or not understood: the answer to a riddle, the meaning of a dream, the secret of a man’s heart, the answer to hard questions.

evidence.note: Samson’s riddle: “if you indeed tell it to me within the seven days of the feast, and find it out”; telling is giving the answer.
He gave the changes of clothes “to those who told the riddle”.
Pharaoh told the dream to the magicians, “and there was none to tell (explain) it to me”.
The king called the magicians “to tell the king his dreams”.
Samson “told her all his heart”: the secret of his strength.
Solomon told the queen of Sheba all her matters; “no matter was hidden from the king that he did not tell her”.
Of the man of God: “perhaps he will tell us our way”.
Jacob to the man who wrestled with him: “Tell, please, your name.”
“That he would tell you the secrets of wisdom.”
“Where were you when I founded the earth? Tell, if you know understanding.”

senses.gloss: own up to, declare openly (a sin, a trouble, a stand)
senses.definition: To bring out into the open what one has done or what one is, by word or by conduct, where it could have been kept back.

evidence.note: Joshua to Achan: וְהַגֶּד־נָא לִי מֶה עָשִׂיתָ אַל־תְּכַחֵד מִמֶּנִּי, “tell me what you have done; do not hide it from me”.
“For I declare my iniquity; I am anxious because of my sin.”
וְחַטָּאתָם כִּסְדֹם הִגִּידוּ לֹא כִחֵדוּ: “their sin, like Sodom, they declare; they do not hide it”.
Joab to David: “you have declared today that commanders and servants are nothing to you”: his weeping has made it plain.
“My distress before his face I declare.”
The man bringing firstfruits: “I declare today to Yahweh your God that I have come to the land.”

senses.definition: Of a witness, to state what he has seen or knows; and to report a man to those who can act against him.

evidence.note: A witness who has seen or known, “if he does not tell, he shall bear his iniquity”.
The thief’s partner “hears the oath and does not tell”: the case of Lev 5:1.
“He who breathes out faithfulness tells righteousness, but a false witness, deceit.”
David: “I knew that day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would surely tell Saul.”
The psalm’s heading: “when Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul”.
Jeremiah’s enemies: “Report him! Let us report him!”
Mordecai learned of the plot and told it to Esther the queen.

senses.gloss: declare (God’s covenant, word or judgment; what he requires)
senses.definition: Of Yahweh, and of those who speak for him (Moses, the priests, the prophets, a father to his son), to set out his covenant, his word, his judgment, a people’s sin or what is good, so that the hearer knows it and is answerable for it.

evidence.note: “He declared to you his covenant which he commanded you to do, the ten words.”
“He declares his word to Jacob, his statutes and his judgments to Israel.”
“He has told you, man, what is good, and what Yahweh seeks from you.”
כֹּה תֹאמַר לְבֵית יַעֲקֹב וְתַגֵּיד לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל: “say” and “tell” side by side.
“You shall tell your son in that day”: the father’s telling of the going out from Egypt.
“Ask your father, and he will tell you; your elders, and they will say to you.”
The priests and the judge “will tell you the word of the judgment”.
“You shall do according to the word which they tell you … according to all that they teach you.”
Moses: “I declare to you today that you will surely perish.”
“Yahweh declares to you that Yahweh will make you a house.”
David inquiring: “Yahweh, God of Israel, tell your servant, please.”
Jeremiah: “every word that Yahweh answers you I will tell you; I will not keep back a word from you.”
“Declare all that you see to the house of Israel.”
The prophet is full of power “to declare to Jacob his transgression”.
“Declare to my people their transgression.”
He who forms mountains and creates wind “declares to man what is his thought”.
A messenger, an interpreter, “to declare to man his uprightness”.
In mockery of divination: “my people asks its wood, and its staff tells it”.

senses.definition: To tell what will happen before it happens. Yahweh sets this as the proof of who is God: he declares the end from the beginning and then does it; the idols and their people are challenged to do the same and cannot; and man does not know what will be after him.

evidence.note: מַגִּיד מֵרֵאשִׁית אַחֲרִית: “declaring from the beginning the end, and from before, things not yet done, saying, My counsel will stand”.
To the idols: “let them bring near and declare to us what will happen … or make us hear the coming things.”
“Declare the things coming afterward, and we will know that you are gods.”
“The former things, behold, they have come, and new things I declare; before they sprout I make you hear them.”
“I declared it to you from then; before it came I made you hear it, lest you say, My idol did them.”
“The former things I declared from then … suddenly I did them, and they came.”
“Who is like me? Let him call and declare it … and the things that will come, let them declare.”
“Did I not make you hear from then, and declare it? And you are my witnesses.”
“Who made this heard from of old, declared it from then? Was it not I, Yahweh?”
“Who declared it from the beginning, that we might know? … there is none declaring.”
Jacob to his sons: “I will tell you what will meet you in the end of the days.”
“I will tell you what is inscribed in the writing of truth.”
“And now I will tell you truth: three more kings will stand in Persia.”
“Even today I declare that I will return double to you.”
“Who will tell man what will be after him under the sun?”
“Man does not know what will be; and what will be after him, who will tell him?”

senses.definition: To make a thing known openly and widely: Yahweh’s praise, righteousness and works, told to the peoples and to the generation to come, and news published in a land. The heavens do it without words.

evidence.note: הַשָּׁמַיִם מְסַפְּרִים כְּבוֹד־אֵל וּמַעֲשֵׂה יָדָיו מַגִּיד הָרָקִיעַ: “recount” and “declare” in parallel.
“Lord, open my lips, and my mouth will declare your praise.”
“Generation to generation will praise your works, and your mighty acts they will declare.”
אַל־תַּגִּידוּ בְגַת אַל־תְּבַשְּׂרוּ בְּחוּצֹת אַשְׁקְלוֹן: “do not tell it in Gath, do not bring the news in the streets of Ashkelon”.
“The heavens declare his righteousness.”
“The heavens declare his righteousness, and all the peoples see his glory.”
“They will come and declare his righteousness to a people yet to be born.”
“Do not forsake me until I declare your arm to a generation.”
“To declare your covenant faithfulness in the morning.”
“Declare among the peoples his deeds.”
All men will fear and declare the work of God.
“The power of his works he declared to his people”: by giving them the nations’ inheritance.
“What profit is there in my blood, in my going down to the pit? Will dust praise you? Will it declare your faithfulness?”: the dead do not.
“Let them declare his praise in the coastlands.”
“With a voice of singing declare, make this heard: Yahweh has redeemed his servant Jacob.”
“Declare in Judah, and in Jerusalem make it heard.”
הַגִּידוּ בַגּוֹיִם וְהַשְׁמִיעוּ … אַל־תְּכַחֵדוּ: “declare among the nations and make it heard … do not hide it”.
“Hear the word of Yahweh, nations, and declare it in the coastlands far off.”

senses.definition: The passive of the hiphil: a matter is brought to someone’s knowledge, the teller unnamed. Most often וַיֻּגַּד לְ “and it was told to” a man, of news; with the infinitive (הֻגֵּד הֻגַּד) “it was fully told”.

evidence.note: The queen of Sheba: “I did not believe the words until I came and my eyes saw; and behold, the half was not told me.”
“Do you not know? Do you not hear? Has it not been told you from the beginning?”
“It was told to Abraham, saying, Milcah also has borne sons.”
It was told Laban on the third day that Jacob had fled.
It was told the king of Egypt that the people had fled.
The Gibeonites: “it was surely told your servants” what Yahweh commanded Moses.
Boaz: הֻגֵּד הֻגַּד לִי, “it has been fully told me, all that you have done”.
Of idolatry in a city: “and it is told you, and you hear, and you inquire well”.
It was told King David that Yahweh had blessed the house of Obed-edom.
“A hard vision has been told to me.”

evidence.locator: Isa.46.10, מַגִּיד → ἀναγγέλλων; Isa.41.23, הַגִּידוּ → ἀναγγείλατε; Isa.42.9, מַגִּיד → ἀναγγελῶ; Psa.19.2, מַגִּיד → ἀναγγέλλει; Gen.3.11, הִגִּיד → ἀνήγγειλεν; ἀναγγέλλω renders the verb ×145

evidence.note: Of the spirit of truth: τὰ ἐρχόμενα ἀναγγελεῖ ὑμῖν, “the coming things it will declare to you”; the thing Isa 41:22–23 asks of the idols.
The woman of Samaria: when Messiah comes, ἀναγγελεῖ ἡμῖν πάντα, “he will declare to us all things”.
Paul did not shrink from declaring (ἀναγγεῖλαι) all the counsel of God.

evidence.locator: Gen.12.18, הִגַּדְתָּ → ἀπήγγειλας; Gen.14.13, וַיַּגֵּד → ἀπήγγειλεν; 2Sa.11.18, וַיַּגֵּד → ἀπήγγειλεν; ἀπαγγέλλω renders the verb ×165

parallels.note: “Make hear”: the regular partner of הִגִּיד where Yahweh declares beforehand, and where news is published.
“Recount”: the heavens recount God’s glory and the expanse declares the work of his hands.
“Bring news”: “do not tell it in Gath, do not bring the news in the streets of Ashkelon”.
“Say”: “thus you shall say to the house of Jacob and tell the sons of Israel”.

opposites.note: “Hide, keep back”: to tell is not to hide.

phrases.gloss: declaring from the beginning the end

words.gloss: in front of, before, in the sight of; opposite, facing; against; (מִנֶּגֶד) away from, at a distance; (כְּנֶגְדּוֹ) corresponding to him
words.summary: About 150 times, always as a preposition or adverb, alone or with לְ, מִן or כְּ. It places one thing in front of another, in full view of it: before a person’s eyes, before an assembly, before Yahweh. From facing comes “opposite” (of position) and, a few times, “against”; מִנֶּגֶד is “from in front of”, so “out of the sight of” or “over against, at a distance”. Where לִפְנֵי is “at the face of”, נֶגֶד lays the weight on being seen (2Sa 12:12, set against “in secret”).

senses.gloss: in front of, before, in the presence of
senses.definition: In front of a person or a company, so that they see what is done: reading the law, praying, paying vows, doing wonders, and being shamed or honoured “before” a people. Set against what is done in secret.

evidence.note: כִּי אַתָּה עָשִׂיתָ בַסָּתֶר וַאֲנִי אֶעֱשֶׂה אֶת־הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה נֶגֶד כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵל וְנֶגֶד הַשָּׁמֶשׁ: “you did it in secret, but I will do this thing before all Israel and before the sun”.
There was not a word that Joshua did not read “before all the assembly of Israel”, women, children and sojourners.
“You shall read this law before all Israel, in their ears.”
Ezra read “before the men and the women and those who could understand”.
Solomon stood before the altar of Yahweh (לִפְנֵי), “in front of all the assembly of Israel” (נֶגֶד).
“Before all your people I will do wonders.”
“Before their fathers he did a wonder, in the land of Egypt.”
“My vows I will pay before those who fear him.”
“My vows to Yahweh I will pay, before all his people.”
“I will speak of your testimonies before kings, and will not be ashamed.”
תַּעֲרֹךְ לְפָנַי שֻׁלְחָן נֶגֶד צֹרְרָי: a table before me, in the sight of my foes.
Saul: “honour me, please, before the elders of my people and before Israel.”
Samuel: “testify against me before Yahweh and before his anointed.”
“Buy it before those sitting here and before the elders of my people.”
Jacob to Laban: “before our brothers, identify what is yours with me.”
The heads of the people hung up “to Yahweh before the sun”.
Yahweh will make righteousness and praise sprout “before all the nations”.
The Egyptians to Joseph: “why should we die before you?”

senses.gloss: before (the eyes or mind); in the sight of (Yahweh)
senses.definition: Of what a man keeps in view: Yahweh, his judgments, his covenant faithfulness, or his own sin; often לְנֶגֶד עֵינָיו “before his eyes”. And of what lies in Yahweh’s view, where nothing is hidden: a man’s ways, desire and iniquities, and the grave itself.

evidence.note: שִׁוִּיתִי יַהְוֶה לְנֶגְדִּי תָמִיד: “I have set Yahweh before me always; because he is at my right hand I will not be moved”. Peter quotes it of the Christ (Act 2:25).
Psa 16:8 quoted: Προωρώμην τὸν κύριον ἐνώπιόν μου διὰ παντός.
“Lord, before you is all my desire, and my sighing is not hidden from you”: before him is the opposite of hidden.
“You have set our iniquities before you, our hidden things in the light of your face.”
“My sin is before me always.”
אֵין־פַּחַד אֱלֹהִים לְנֶגֶד עֵינָיו: “there is no dread of God before his eyes”; quoted in Rom 3:18.
Psa 36:2 quoted: οὐκ ἔστιν φόβος θεοῦ ἀπέναντι τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτῶν.
“Your covenant faithfulness is before my eyes.”
“All his judgments are before me.”
The violent “have not set God before them”; so Psa 86:14.
“I will not set before my eyes a worthless thing.”
“All my ways are before you.”
“The grave and destruction are before Yahweh; how much more the hearts of the sons of man!”
“Naked is the grave before him, and there is no covering for destruction.”
“Their deeds surround them; they are before my face.”
To Zion: “your walls are before me continually.”
“Our transgressions are many before you.”
David’s throne “as the sun before me”.
“A form was before my eyes.”
“Is not food cut off before our eyes?”
“Your life will hang before you”: in doubt, always in view.

senses.definition: Of where one thing stands in relation to another: facing it, across from it, in line with it. So Israel camped facing the mountain, each man built the wall opposite his own house, and the Levites sang with their brothers standing opposite them.

evidence.note: “Israel camped there in front of the mountain.”
“The people crossed over opposite Jericho.”
Joshua looked, “and behold, a man standing in front of him, his sword drawn in his hand”.
Jedaiah repaired “opposite his house”; so through the chapter (3:23, 28, 29).
Watches set, “each one in front of his house”.
Bakbukiah and Unni, their brothers, “opposite them in the watches”.
וַאֲחֵיהֶם לְנֶגְדָּם … מִשְׁמָר לְעֻמַּת מִשְׁמָר: brothers opposite them, watch over against watch.
Israel camped opposite Aram “like two little flocks of goats”.
The third captain knelt on his knees in front of Elijah.
“Opening opposite opening.”
They lived in Jerusalem “opposite their brothers”.
Daniel spoke “to the one standing in front of me”.

senses.definition: With a suffix naming the one who moves or looks: in the direction he faces, straight on.

evidence.note: The wall will fall, “and the people shall go up, each man straight before him” (אִישׁ נֶגְדּוֹ); so 6:20.
“Through the breaches you will go out, each woman straight before her.”
עֵינֶיךָ לְנֹכַח יַבִּיטוּ וְעַפְעַפֶּיךָ יַיְשִׁרוּ נֶגְדֶּךָ: “let your eyes look straight on, and your eyelids be straight before you”.
The measuring line will go out “straight on” to the hill Gareb.
Esau: “let us journey and go, and I will go in front of you” (לְנֶגְדֶּךָ).

senses.gloss: against, in opposition to; in comparison with
senses.definition: A few times facing becomes standing against: a prince who withstands, witnesses renewed against a man, two who stand against one. Before Yahweh no wisdom stands, and the nations set before him are as nothing.

evidence.note: “The prince of the kingdom of Persia stood against me (עֹמֵד לְנֶגְדִּי) twenty-one days, and behold, Michael … came to help me.”
“If one overpowers him, the two will stand against him.”
“You renew your witnesses against me.”
“There is no wisdom and no understanding and no counsel against Yahweh” (לְנֶגֶד יַהְוֶה): none that can stand before him.
The angel of Yahweh to Balaam: “I came out as an adversary, for the way is headlong before me.”
“All the nations are as nothing before him”: set beside him and measured.
“My lifetime is as nothing before you.”

senses.gloss: (מִנֶּגֶד) from before, out of the sight of; over against, at a distance, aloof
senses.definition: With מִן: away from in front of someone, so out of his sight (מִנֶּגֶד עֵינַי “from before my eyes”); or, of one who stands or sits, off in front and apart, where he can see and is not near: at a distance, aloof.

evidence.note: Hagar sat מִנֶּגֶד, “far off, about a bowshot”, so as not to see the child die.
Fifty sons of the prophets “stood opposite, at a distance” (מִנֶּגֶד מֵרָחוֹק); they see him from there in 2:15.
Moses: “from in front you will see the land, but you will not go there.”
“My friends stand aloof from my plague, and my near ones stand far off.”
Edom: “in the day you stood aloof … you also were as one of them.”
“You yourself would have stood aloof.”
The tribes camp “over against, around the tent of meeting”.
“Remove the evil of your deeds from before my eyes.”
“I am driven out from before your eyes.”
“I am cut off from before your eyes.”
לֹא נִסְתְּרוּ מִלְּפָנָי וְלֹא־נִצְפַּן עֲוֺנָם מִנֶּגֶד עֵינָי: “not hidden from my face, nor is their iniquity concealed from before my eyes”.
“If they hide from before my eyes on the floor of the sea.”
“Turn your eyes away from me.”
Gideon “cast his life in front”: risked it.

senses.gloss: (כְּנֶגְדּוֹ) as in front of him: corresponding to him, his counterpart
senses.definition: Only of the woman, twice: a helper “as in front of him”, one who stands facing the man as his like and match. The context fixes it: the man is alone, every beast is brought and named, and among them none is found that is כְּנֶגְדּוֹ; the one who is, is built from his own side, “bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh”.

evidence.note: לֹא־טוֹב הֱיוֹת הָאָדָם לְבַדּוֹ אֶעֱשֶׂהּ־לּוֹ עֵזֶר כְּנֶגְדּוֹ: “it is not good for the man to be alone; I will make for him a helper corresponding to him”.
The man named every beast, “but for the man there was not found a helper corresponding to him”.
What the man says when she is brought: “this, now, is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh”.

evidence.locator: Psa.51.5 (LXX 50:5), נֶגְדִּי → ἐνώπιόν μου; 1Sa.12.3, נֶגֶד → ἐνώπιον; ἐνώπιον renders נֶגֶד ×19

evidence.note: Psa 16:8 quoted: “I saw the Lord before me (ἐνώπιόν μου) always”.
“No creature is hidden before him (ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ), but all things are naked … to his eyes”: the thought of Job 26:6 and Pro 15:11.

evidence.locator: Psa.36.2 (LXX 35:2), נֶגֶד → ἀπέναντι; ἀπέναντι renders נֶגֶד ×16

evidence.note: Psa 36:2 quoted: “there is no fear of God before (ἀπέναντι) their eyes”.

evidence.locator: Gen.31.32, נֶגֶד → ἐναντίον; 2Sa.12.12, נֶגֶד → ἐναντίον; Psa.119.46 (LXX 118:46), נֶגֶד → ἐναντίον; ἐναντίον renders נֶגֶד ×27

evidence.note: God gave Joseph favour and wisdom “before (ἐναντίον) Pharaoh”.

evidence.locator: Exo.19.2, נֶגֶד → κατέναντι; Neh.3.10, נֶגֶד → κατέναντι; κατέναντι renders נֶגֶד ×15

parallels.note: “At the face of”: the two stand side by side, לִפְנֵי of the nearer presence and נֶגֶד of those looking on.

evidence.note: מִלְּפָנָי beside מִנֶּגֶד עֵינָי.

parallels.note: “Straight in front”: eyes that look לְנֹכַח and eyelids straight נֶגְדֶּךָ.
“Alongside, over against”: brothers לְנֶגְדָּם, watch לְעֻמַּת watch.

opposites.note: “Secret, hiding place”: done in secret, against done נֶגֶד all Israel; and what is נֶגֶד Yahweh is not hidden (נִסְתַּר) from him.

phrases.gloss: from before my eyes, out of my sight
before the sun: in broad daylight, publicly

words.gloss: leader, ruler (the one in front); chief officer; noble
words.summary: Forty-four times. The one in front of a people or a body of men. In Samuel and Kings it is the word for the man Yahweh picks out and sets over his people: Saul is anointed נָגִיד before he is made king, and David, Solomon, Jeroboam, Baasha and Hezekiah are each called it by Yahweh. In Chronicles and Nehemiah it is also any chief officer: of the house of God, of a tribe, of the treasuries, of the army. Scripture nowhere explains the word; that it is “one in front” rests on נֶגֶד, on its use of leaders “over” (עַל) a people, and on the Aramaic נָגוֹדָא “leader, guide”.

senses.gloss: leader, ruler over Yahweh’s people (appointed by him)
senses.definition: The man whom Yahweh chooses, takes from among the people and commands to be over them: נָגִיד עַל־עַמִּי יִשְׂרָאֵל. It is given by anointing, before and apart from the acclaim that makes a king, and it is Yahweh’s word for the king as his appointee, who shepherds a people that remains Yahweh’s.

evidence.note: Yahweh to Samuel: “you shall anoint him as leader over my people Israel, and he will save my people from the hand of the Philistines.”
Samuel poured the oil on Saul’s head: “has not Yahweh anointed you as leader over his inheritance?”
“Yahweh has sought for himself a man according to his heart, and Yahweh has commanded him to be leader over his people.”
אַתָּה תִרְעֶה אֶת־עַמִּי אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאַתָּה תִּהְיֶה לְנָגִיד עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵל: “you will shepherd my people Israel, and you will be leader over Israel”; so 1Ch 11:2.
“I took you from the pasture, from following the flock, to be leader over my people, over Israel”; so 1Ch 17:7.
David: Yahweh “chose me above your father … to appoint me leader over the people of Yahweh”.
Abigail: when Yahweh “has appointed you leader over Israel”.
David of Solomon: “him I have commanded to be leader over Israel and over Judah.”
They made Solomon king a second time “and anointed him to Yahweh as leader”.
To Jeroboam: “I raised you up from the midst of the people and made you leader over my people Israel”; to Baasha, “from the dust” (1Ki 16:2).
“Hezekiah, the leader of my people.”
“He chose Judah as leader”; so 1Ch 5:2, “from him came a leader”.

Of the one in whom the sure covenant faithfulnesses of David stand: הֵן עֵד לְאוּמִּים נְתַתִּיו נָגִיד וּמְצַוֵּה לְאֻמִּים, “a witness to peoples I have given him, a leader and commander of peoples”.

עַד־מָשִׁיחַ נָגִיד: “until an anointed one, a leader”: seven sevens and sixty-two sevens from the word to restore and build Jerusalem. No article: the two nouns stand side by side, the anointing and the office as in 1Sa 9:16; 10:1.
The chief priests’ answer joins Mic 5:1 to 2Sa 5:2: ἐκ σοῦ γὰρ ἐξελεύσεται ἡγούμενος ὅστις ποιμανεῖ τὸν λαόν μου τὸν Ἰσραήλ.

senses.gloss: chief officer (of the house of God, a tribe, the treasuries, the army, the palace)
senses.definition: The man at the head of a body or a charge: the chief priest as “leader of the house of God”, the head of a tribe or of a division, the officer over the treasuries, the commander of a fortress, the steward of the king’s house, a foreign king’s officers.

evidence.note: Azariah, of the line of Zadok, “leader of the house of God”; so Neh 11:11 and 2Ch 31:13.
Hilkiah, Zechariah and Jehiel, “leaders of the house of God”: more than one at a time.
Pashhur the priest was “chief officer in the house of Yahweh”.
“Phinehas the son of Eleazar was leader over them formerly; Yahweh was with him.”
“Jehoiada, the leader of Aaron’s house.”
“Over the tribes of Israel: of the Reubenites, the leader was Eliezer.”
Shebuel, “leader over the treasuries”.
David consulted the captains of thousands and hundreds, “every leader”.
Rehoboam put “leaders” (commanders) in the fortresses.
He set Abijah as head, “as leader among his brothers, to make him king”.
Zebadiah, “the leader of the house of Judah, for every matter of the king”, beside the head priest for every matter of Yahweh.
Azrikam, “leader of the house”: over the palace.
Conaniah the Levite was leader over the contributions, and Shimei his brother second.
The angel cut off every warrior, “leader and commander” in the camp of Assyria.

senses.gloss: prince, ruler, noble (in general; of other nations)
senses.definition: A ruler or great man without reference to Israel’s throne: the ruler of Tyre, the princes whose spirit God cuts off, the nobles who fall silent before Job. Twice in Daniel of a ruler to come. Once the plural is used of words: “princely things”.

evidence.note: “Say to the leader of Tyre … you are man and not God.”
“He cuts off the spirit of princes; he is feared by the kings of the earth”: נְגִידִים beside kings.
“The voice of nobles was hushed.”
“Like a prince I would approach him.”
“A ruler lacking understanding is great in oppressions.”
After the anointed one is cut off: וְהָעִיר וְהַקֹּדֶשׁ יַשְׁחִית עַם נָגִיד הַבָּא, “the city and the sanctuary the people of a leader who comes will destroy”.
“Also a leader of covenant” will be broken.
Wisdom: “hear, for I speak נְגִידִים”, princely or noble things, beside “upright things”. Only here of words.

evidence.locator: 2Sa.5.2, נָגִיד → ἡγούμενον; 1Ch.11.2, נָגִיד → ἡγούμενον; ἡγέομαι renders נָגִיד ×21

evidence.note: “Out of you will come a leader (ἡγούμενος) who will shepherd my people Israel”: the words of 2Sa 5:2 joined to Mic 5:1.
Pharaoh set Joseph as ἡγούμενον over Egypt and all his house.
“Remember those leading you (τῶν ἡγουμένων ὑμῶν), who spoke to you the word of God.”

evidence.locator: 1Sa.9.16, נָגִיד → ἄρχοντα; Isa.55.4, נָגִיד → ἄρχοντα; ἄρχων renders נָגִיד ×8

parallels.note: “King”: the same man is anointed נָגִיד and made king; princes stand beside the kings of the earth.
“Captain, commander”: leader and commander in the Assyrian camp; captains of thousands and every leader.

phrases.gloss: leader of the house of God

words.summary: Biblical Aramaic, once only (Dan 6:11); elsewhere Daniel’s Aramaic uses קֳדָם and לָקֳבֵל for “before”. One use is little to fix a word by, but it is the Hebrew preposition’s sense of position. Its key counts 53 tokens because the Hebrew נֶגֶד is spelt the same; only Dan 6:11 is Aramaic.

senses.definition: Of windows: opening in the direction of a place.

evidence.note: וְכַוִּין פְּתִיחָן לֵהּ בְּעִלִּיתֵהּ נֶגֶד יְרוּשְׁלֶם: Daniel’s windows in his upper room were open “toward Jerusalem”, and there he knelt three times a day.

words.summary: Biblical Aramaic, once only (Dan 7:10), of a river. It is the common Aramaic verb “draw, pull, stretch out”, which the Peshitta has for drawing a net and for the Father drawing men; a stream is water drawn out along its course. How this Aramaic sense joins the Hebrew “be in front” is not settled: the meeting point is leading, since the one who draws others after him goes in front (Peshitta נָגוֹדָא “guide”, Hebrew נָגִיד).

senses.definition: Of a river: to run out along its course.

evidence.note: נְהַר דִּי־נוּר נָגֵד וְנָפֵק מִן־קֳדָמוֹהִי: “a river of fire was flowing and coming out from before him”; “flowing” is paired with “coming out”.

words.gloss: draw, pull, drag; lead aside; withdraw; (pael) scourge (Peshitta)
words.summary: The Peshitta’s verb for drawing: a net to land, a man aside, men to court, and the Father drawing men to the Son; where the Greek has ἕλκω, ἑλκύω and σύρω. In the pael it is to scourge, where the Greek has μαστιγόω and φραγελλόω. The step from drawing to scourging is not shown by scripture; the Aramaic noun for the lash is a strap, a thing drawn out.

stems.gloss: draw, pull, drag; lead aside; withdraw

senses.definition: To make something or someone come along after one: hauling a net, dragging men by force, and, of God and of his son, bringing men to them.

evidence.note: Simon went up “and drew the net to land, full of great fish”; so 21:6, 8.
“No man can come to me unless the Father who sent me draws him”; the next verse says how: “they will all be taught of God”.
“And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw every man to me.”
They seized Paul and Silas “and dragged and brought them to the marketplace”.
The rich “drag you to the house of judgment”.

senses.definition: To take a person apart from others; with נַפְשֵׁהּ “himself”, to draw back.

evidence.note: Jesus “led him from the crowd by himself”.
The commander took the young man by the hand “and led him to one side”.
When they came from James, Cephas “withdrew himself and separated”.

senses.gloss: be drawn away; be led along
senses.definition: The passive of the peal: to be drawn by something, whether a man’s own desire or the holy spirit moving the prophets.

evidence.note: “Each man is tempted by his own desire, and he lusts and is drawn away.”
Prophecy never came by man’s will, “but holy men of God spoke as they were led along by holy spirit”.

senses.definition: To beat with a whip or rods as a punishment: of Jesus by Pilate, of the apostles by the council, and of the Lord’s chastening of his sons.

evidence.note: Pilate “scourged Jesus with whips and delivered him to be crucified”; so Jhn 19:1.
Foretold: “they will mock him and scourge him and crucify him.”
The council called the apostles and scourged them.
Pro 3:12 quoted: “whom the Lord loves he chastens, and he scourges the sons in whom he delights.”

senses.definition: The passive of the pael.

evidence.note: “In their synagogues you will be scourged.”
“Three times I was scourged with rods.”

words.summary: The agent noun of נְגַד: one who draws others after him, a guide. In the Peshitta only in Jesus’ words about blind guides (Greek ὁδηγός). It is the Aramaic counterpart of Hebrew נָגִיד.

senses.gloss: guide, one who leads the way
senses.definition: One who goes in front and leads others along the way; used of the Pharisees and scribes as teachers of the people.

evidence.note: “They are blind guides of the blind; and if a blind man leads a blind man, both will fall into a pit.”
“Woe to you, blind guides.”

words.summary: The noun of the pael: the blow of the scourge, and the weal it leaves. Four times in the Peshitta.

senses.definition: A flogging, and the wounds left by it.

evidence.note: The jailer “washed them from their stripes”.
The commander ordered that Paul “be questioned by scourging”.
“In stripes, in bonds.”
Others “entered into mockings and scourgings”.

words.summary: The agent noun of the pael, once in the Peshitta (Greek βασανιστής); one use fixes little beyond its form.

senses.definition: One whose work is to scourge prisoners.

evidence.note: The lord “delivered him to the scourgers until he should pay all that he owed”.

cognates.gloss: be or become apparent, manifest, plain, evident; (of a road) be conspicuous
cognates.note: Arabic j answers to Hebrew g. Said of a thing, an affair or a road that stands out plainly to view: the sense of Hebrew נֶגֶד, and the hiphil הִגִּיד is its causative, to make a matter plain before someone. Lane lists this sense apart from the root’s commoner ones (overcome; be courageous; aid).

evidence.note: “نَجَدَ … inf. n. نُجُودٌ, It (a thing, or an affair,) was, or became, apparent, manifest, plain, or evident. … It (a road) was, or became, apparent, manifest, conspicous, or plain.”

cognates.gloss: high land that stands over against one; an elevated, conspicuous road; a thing apparent, manifest
cognates.note: The noun of the same root: what rises in front of a traveller and is seen. Lane’s definition of the land so called uses the very notion of נֶגֶד, “standing over against one”; hence the name of the Najd, the high country of Arabia.

evidence.note: “High, or elevated, land or country … elevated land, like a mountain, standing over against one and intercepting his view of what is behind it … An elevated road: or an elevated and conspicuous road … A thing, or an affair, apparent, manifest, plain, or evident.”

cognates.note: The same noun as Arabic najd, in one Sabaean inscription. It shows the root in South Arabia with the Arabic noun’s sense of high ground, not with the Hebrew’s “in front”; kept as possible for that reason.

evidence.note: “HIGHLAND, PLATEAU [CAr najd id. …] Ir 12/5: ngd M ‘on the plateau of M.’” (OCR read; the page is counted from the scan’s page footers after the printed 289, PDF not rendered).

cognates.note: On the Nora stone from Sardinia, of the commander of a garrison: the same noun as Hebrew נָגִיד, in its sense of an officer at the head of a body of men.

evidence.note: “[Heb. nagîd] n.m. LEADER, COMMANDER … ‘Its commandant (leader) is Pumay.’” (OCR read; PDF not rendered).

cognates.note: A Neo-Punic preposition, of worshippers praying “facing heaven”: the Hebrew נֶגֶד, used as Daniel’s windows are “toward Jerusalem”. The text is partly restored.

evidence.note: “[Heb. neged] prep. OPPOSITE, FACING … ‘facing Heaven they prayed’” (OCR read; PDF not rendered; the first letter of the word is restored in the inscription).

cognates.gloss: stretch, draw, pull; lead, guide; flow; (pael) lash (Jewish Aramaic)
cognates.note: The Targums’ and Talmud’s verb, with the range the Peshitta shows: draw and pull, lead the way, flow (of honey, of streams), and in the pael lash. It is the verb of Dan 7:10.

evidence.note: “to stretch; to draw, pull, spread … to guide, rule. Targ. Ruth I, 1 … to grow long; to be drawn, follow after; to flow … Pa. to lash, punish.”

cognates.note: The Targum’s word for the leaders of the tribes in 1Ch 27:16, where the Hebrew has נָגִיד, and for the judges; a proverb uses it of the animal that leads the flock. The leader is the one who draws the rest after him.

evidence.note: “esp. ruler, judge. Targ. I Chr. XXVII, 16. Targ. Jud. II, 18 … when the shepherd is angry with his flock, he makes the leader blind.”

cognates.gloss: leather strap, lash; lashing, punishment (Jewish Aramaic)
cognates.note: The lash is named as a strap, a thing drawn out, from נְגַד; from it comes the pael “lash”. This is the only evidence found for how the Aramaic verb came to mean scourge.

evidence.note: “(נְגַד; cmp. מִשְׁכָא) leather-strap, lash; trnsf. lashing, punishment.”

doctrine.statement: Yahweh calls the gods of the nations to one test: “declare to us what will happen … declare the things coming afterward, and we will know that you are gods” (Isa 41:22–23), and none answers: “there is none declaring” (Isa 41:26). Of himself he says, “new things I declare; before they sprout I make you hear them” (Isa 42:9); “I declared it to you from then, before it came I made you hear it, lest you say, My idol did them” (Isa 48:5); “declaring from the beginning the end … saying, My counsel will stand” (Isa 46:10). Israel are his witnesses that he did (Isa 44:8). Man cannot do it: “what will be after him, who will tell him?” (Ecc 10:14). So Daniel is told what is “inscribed in the writing of truth” (Dan 10:21), and Jesus promises his apostles that the spirit of truth “will declare to you the coming things” (Jhn 16:13); prophecy did not come by man’s will, but men spoke as holy spirit led them (2Pe 1:21). From the verses: declaring the future and bringing it to pass is the mark by which Yahweh is known to be God alone, and fulfilled prophecy is the evidence he himself offers.

A נָגִיד over Yahweh’s people is a man Yahweh chooses and raises from among them: Saul “from the land of Benjamin” (1Sa 9:16), David “from the pasture, from following the flock” (2Sa 7:8), “a man according to his heart” (1Sa 13:14), who is to shepherd a people that remains Yahweh’s (2Sa 5:2). Yahweh promised David a house (2Sa 7:11), and Isaiah speaks of the one in whom “the sure covenant faithfulnesses of David” stand as given “a witness to peoples, a leader and commander of peoples” (Isa 55:3–4); Paul applies those words to the raising of Jesus from the dead (Act 13:34). The chief priests answered Herod from the prophets that out of Bethlehem would come “a leader who will shepherd my people Israel” (Mat 2:6), and the angel told Mary that God would give her son “the throne of David his father, and he will reign over the house of Jacob for ever” (Luk 1:32–33). From the verses: the Christ is the leader of David’s line, a man chosen and anointed by God as David was, raised from the dead to hold David’s throne over Israel and to command the peoples.

Gabriel tells Daniel that from the going out of the word to restore and build Jerusalem “until an anointed one, a leader” there are seven sevens and sixty-two sevens (Dan 9:25); that after the sixty-two sevens “an anointed one will be cut off, and there is nothing for him”; and that “the city and the sanctuary the people of a leader who comes will destroy”, with war and desolations decreed to the end (Dan 9:26). The words מָשִׁיחַ and נָגִיד are those of Saul’s and David’s appointment (1Sa 10:1; 2Sa 5:2–3): the king of Yahweh’s choosing. Jesus sent his hearers to Daniel for the desolation of the holy place (Mat 24:15), said that Jerusalem would be surrounded by armies, its desolation near, and trodden down by the nations (Luk 21:20, 24), and in his parable of those who killed the king’s son, “the king sent his armies and destroyed those murderers and burned their city” (Mat 22:7). From the verses: the anointed leader is Jesus, cut off in death at the time Daniel was given; and the destruction of the city and the sanctuary that followed came by the Roman armies in AD 70, as he said it would.

What is נֶגֶד Yahweh is in his full view. “All my ways are before you” (Psa 119:168); “before you is all my desire, and my sighing is not hidden from you” (Psa 38:10); “you have set our iniquities before you, our hidden things in the light of your face” (Psa 90:8); Israel’s iniquity is not concealed “from before my eyes” (Jer 16:17), and those who hide from before his eyes on the floor of the sea are found there (Amo 9:3). Even the grave is so: “the grave and destruction are before Yahweh; how much more the hearts of the sons of man” (Pro 15:11); “naked is the grave before him” (Job 26:6). Hebrews says the same: “no creature is hidden before him, but all things are naked and laid open to the eyes of him to whom we give account” (Heb 4:13). The wicked man is the one with “no dread of God before his eyes” (Psa 36:2; Rom 3:18); the faithful one says, “I have set Yahweh before me always” (Psa 16:8). From the verses: God sees every way and thought of man, the dead in the grave are not out of his sight or reach, and a man’s part is to keep God in his own view.

David pleads for his life on the ground that the dead cannot declare: “What profit is there in my blood, in my going down to the pit? Will dust praise you? Will it declare your faithfulness?” (Psa 30:10). The same is asked of the grave: “Is your covenant faithfulness recounted in the tomb, your faithfulness in destruction?” (Psa 88:12), and stated outright: “the dead do not praise Yah, nor any who go down to silence” (Psa 115:17). So the psalmist asks to be kept alive “until I declare your arm to a generation” (Psa 71:18). From the verses: a dead man is dust and silent; declaring God’s praise belongs to the living, and to the dead only when they are raised.

God said, “It is not good for the man to be alone; I will make for him a helper כְּנֶגְדּוֹ”, as in front of him (Gen 2:18). Every beast and bird was then brought to the man and named, “but for the man there was not found a helper corresponding to him” (Gen 2:20): living souls though they were, none stood before him as his like. The one who did was built from his own side, and he said, “this, now, is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh” (Gen 2:23); therefore a man clings to his wife and they become one flesh (Gen 2:24). Paul reads the order of the making, “the woman for the man” (1Co 11:9), and adds that in the Lord neither is without the other (1Co 11:11). From the verses: the woman is the man’s counterpart, of his own nature and facing him as no animal can, made for him and joined to him as one flesh.

James says, “Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted by God” (Jas 1:13), and then where temptation does come from: “each man is tempted by his own desire, and is drawn away” (Jas 1:14), the Peshitta’s verb being the passive of נְגַד, to be pulled along as a net is pulled; “and this desire conceives and bears sin, and sin, when it is full grown, bears death” (Jas 1:15). From the verses: what draws a man into sin is his own desire, within him, and the end of that road is death.

note: Drafted 2026-11-15. Root key נגד as the database and BDB key it; no other entry has it. Words and keys: נָגַד n.ar.aa (hiphil 335, hophal 35), נֶגֶד n.ar.ab, נָגִיד n.ar.ac, Aramaic נֶגֶד xn.ab.ab (the key counts 53 tokens by spelling; only Dan 6:11 is Aramaic, and n.ar.ab likewise includes Dan 6:11), Aramaic נְגַד xn.ab.aa (Dan 7:10). No personal name is formed from the root in the text, so no name entries. Verse numbers are the Hebrew text’s (Psa 36:2 = English 36:1; Psa 51:5 = 51:3; Psa 30:10 = 30:9; Dan 6:11 = 6:10; Mic 5:1 = 5:2). Peshitta: SEDRA root 1136 נגד, lexemes 1899 verb, 1901 נָגוֹדָא, 1900 נֶגְדָּא, 1898 מְנַגְּדָנָא; all four entered; the Syriac lemmas’ pointing is mine from the forms in the text and should be checked. Open question for review: how Aramaic “draw, pull, flow, scourge” joins Hebrew “be in front, make known”. The entry offers leading (נָגוֹדָא, נָגִיד) as the meeting point and says so in the words’ summaries; it may be that two older roots share the spelling, but no cognate shows a sound difference (the root has no merged letter). Dan 9:26 עַם נָגִיד הַבָּא: the doctrine item states the AD 70 destruction by the Roman armies and cites Mat 22:7 (“his armies”); it does not decide whether the “leader who comes” is the Roman commander or the Messiah whose armies they are, since the verse alone does not. Dan 11:22 נְגִיד בְּרִית is listed without identification. Cognate locators: Krahmalkov p. 324 and Biella p. 291 are from the scans’ OCR text only (no PDF renderer here); Biella’s page is counted from page footers after the printed 289 and needs checking against the PDF. Leads not followed (no verified locator): Ge'ez nagada “travel, trade” (Dillmann, Leslau); Old Aramaic ngd “officer” in the Sefire treaties (KAI 224); Arabic najīd “courageous” (Lane p. 2768, verified but not entered since it shares no sense with the Hebrew); Syriac dictionaries (Payne Smith, Brockelmann) for ܢܓܕ; CAL for the Aramaic. Oracc has no Akkadian ngd. Not entered from the Peshitta verb’s uses: Act 22:29 (infinitive, “to scourge”), Act 16:22–23, 37; 22:25; Mat 10:17; 23:34; Mrk 10:34; 15:15; Luk 18:33, all pael “scourge” as cited.
